title: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
author: Ilya Gusev
description: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS…
summary: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews.
takeaways: These results provide evidence that LLM-flagged reviews of one paper are less distinct from each other than unflagged reviews, and suggest that the diversity of critiques among reviews of a single paper is falling.
A third ICLR review of a paper added 5.46 new problems to the other two in 2027, against 6.12 in 2026.
We apply MELD, a detector of LLM-generated text, to all reviews.
